title: Plain format names and handler ids in the compiler, runtime, kb and workspace-runtime documents
summary: Documents, receipts and wire formats name themselves plainly beside an integer formatVersion (1) instead of carrying their version in the name: compiled-harness, task-context-declaration, task-capture-selection, position-body, position-packet, delivery-view, packet-receipt, method-bytes, kb-package, kb-selection, kb-portable, kb-citation, kb-snapshot, kb-foundation, captured-resources, authoring-resources, authoring-index, authoring-view, installed-adapter, retained-store, lifecycle-profile, lifecycle-event, lifecycle-context, lifecycle-context-segment, prepared-lifecycle-context, native-context, projection-descriptor, projection-manifest, projection-result, projection-catalog, lowering-map and managed-draft. The prose projection profiles are host.claude-prose and host.codex-prose, and the handlers corpus-inspect, candidate-validate and draft-publish; candidateValidation, managedPublication and Corpus return an adapters map that answers the plain and the original handler. Everything written before this keeps working: every reader lists the original ia.<name>.v1 literals (and iakb.portable.v1, inventarch.method-bytes/1, ia.host.<name>-prose.v1) explicitly, accepts them, and verifies the body as written, digest included, while every new write is plain; compileHarness takes the stamp of a retained compilation so rebuilding it reproduces its digest. A format that is neither is refused. Breaking: every new document, receipt and wire answer (ia position and ia next JSON, the packet receipt, the compiled harness, the kb package, selection and citation, KB_FORMAT) carries the plain format with formatVersion 1, so consumers that matched the old literal must read formatVersion. The ia-workspace-locations-2 registry file and the method-closures-v1 store folder keep their names.
